# Tools reference

What this page covers: every MCP tool mesa-mcp registers at import time,
grouped by prefix and listed alphabetically within each group. Field
names, types, defaults and descriptions are copied from each tool's
Pydantic input model, which is also what clients receive as the tool's
`inputSchema` (JSON Schema 2020-12). A connected client's `tools/list`
response is the authoritative, live version of this page.

**52 built-in tools:** 35 `ds_*`, 6 `mesa_ols_*`, 2 ontology `mesa_avu_*`,
4 DataCite (`mesa_datacite_*` and `mesa_avu_apply_datacite`), 3
`mesa_ducklake_*`, 2 `mesa_policy_*`.

## How results and errors come back

- Each tool returns a JSON object. The server sends it both as
  `structuredContent` and as a single JSON text block. Only `ds_ping`
  also publishes an `outputSchema` today.
- A failure comes back with `isError: true` and
  `{"error": {"code", "message", "details"}}`. Common codes:
  `invalid_argument` (bad input), `unauthenticated`, `forbidden` (path
  outside your accessible paths, or an anonymous caller), `not_found`,
  `irods_error`, `upstream_error` (OLS), `ducklake_disabled`.
- Each tool definition carries `_meta["io.mesa/surface"]`: `irods`,
  `ontology`, `datacite`, `history`, `policy` (or a plugin's own family),
  so a client can group tools without parsing names.
- `tools/list` is marked cacheable for 5 minutes (`ttlMs` 300000, public).

## Plugin tools

Packages can add tools through the `mesa_mcp.tools` entry-point group;
they are loaded when the server starts and are not counted above.

- `mesa_croissant_*` (MLCommons Croissant metadata) from
  [idss-mesa/mesa-croissant](https://github.com/idss-mesa/mesa-croissant),
  installed with the `croissant` extra.
- `mesa_decide_*` from mesa-anyjev, which the MESA installer adds.

A plugin that fails to import is skipped with a warning, unless
`MESA_MCP_SERVER__STRICT_PLUGINS=1` makes that a startup error.

## Regenerating this list

```bash
python -c "
import mesa_mcp.server as s
for spec in sorted(s.get_registered_tools(), key=lambda t: t.name):
    print(spec.name)
"
```

Importing `mesa_mcp.server` imports every built-in tool package. Plugin
tools appear only after `mesa_mcp.server.load_plugins()`.

## ds_*: CyVerse Data Store (iRODS)

Mirrors the tool surface of [cyverse/irods-mcp-server](https://github.com/cyverse/irods-mcp-server) (same names and input shapes), plus ticket lifecycle, rule and policy tools, `ds_add_avus`, `ds_search_metadata`, `ds_get_metadata` and `ds_ping`. Every path argument is checked against the caller's accessible paths (home and shared) and fails with `forbidden` otherwise; the search tools instead drop results outside those paths. `ds_add_avu`, `ds_add_avus` and `ds_delete_avu` mirror path-target AVU changes into the AVU history (see [DuckLake integration](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/dev/ducklake-integration/)).

### `ds_add_avu`

Add a new AVU (attribute-value-unit) to a file (data-object), directory (collection), resource, or user.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `target_type` (required) | `"path"` \| `"resource"` \| `"user"` |  | The type of the target to add AVU. It can be 'path', 'resource', or 'user'. |
| `target` (required) | string |  | The target to add AVU. Path for 'path' target_type, resource name for 'resource' target_type, and user name for 'user' target_type. |
| `attribute` (required) | string |  | The attribute of the AVU to add. |
| `value` (required) | string |  | The value of the AVU to add. |
| `unit` | string | `""` | The unit of the AVU to add. Default is an empty string. |

Only `path` targets are mirrored into the AVU history. On a mirror failure the result carries `partial_failure` with code `ducklake_mirror_failed`; the iRODS write stands.

### `ds_add_avus`

Add MULTIPLE AVUs to one data-object/collection in a single call and mirror them all into DuckLake as ONE snapshot (efficient bulk tagging).

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `target_type` | `"path"` | `"path"` | — |
| `target` (required) | string |  | iRODS path of the data-object or collection. |
| `avus` (required) | array of AvuItem |  | AVUs to add in one batched call. |

Each `avus` item is `{attribute, value, unit}` (`unit` defaults to `""`). All AVUs are mirrored as one history snapshot.

### `ds_copy_file`

Copy a file (data-object) or directory (collection) to a new location.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `source_path` (required) | string |  | The path to the source file (data-object) or directory (collection). If directory path is given, the entire directory and its contents will be copied. |
| `destination_path` (required) | string |  | The new, complete path to copy the file (data-object) or directory (collection) to, including its new name. The path must not already exist. |

### `ds_create_ticket`

Create a read or write iRODS ticket on a data object or collection. Returns the ticket string plus the restrictions that were applied. Anonymous users may not create tickets.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `path` (required) | string |  | The iRODS path the ticket grants access to. |
| `mode` (required) | `"read"` \| `"write"` |  | Ticket access mode: 'read' or 'write'. |
| `uses_allowed` | integer \| null | `null` | Maximum number of times this ticket may be used. |
| `expiry` | string \| null | `null` | ISO-8601 timestamp at which the ticket expires. |
| `write_byte_limit` | integer \| null | `null` | Maximum bytes that may be written via this ticket (write tickets only). |
| `host_restriction` | string \| null | `null` | Restrict ticket usage to clients connecting from this host. |
| `user_restriction` | string \| null | `null` | Restrict ticket usage to this iRODS user. |

### `ds_delete_avu`

Delete an AVU (attribute-value-unit) from a file, directory, resource, or user.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `target_type` (required) | `"path"` \| `"resource"` \| `"user"` |  | The type of the target to delete AVU. It can be 'path', 'resource', or 'user'. |
| `target` (required) | string |  | The target to delete AVU. Path for 'path' target_type, resource name for 'resource' target_type, and user name for 'user' target_type. |
| `id` | integer | `0` | The ID of the AVU to delete. |
| `attribute` | string | `""` | The attribute of the AVU to delete. This field can be ignored if ID is provided. |
| `value` | string | `""` | The value of the AVU to delete. Default is an empty string. |
| `unit` | string | `""` | The unit of the AVU to delete. Default is an empty string. |

Only `path` targets are mirrored into the AVU history, as an `op=delete` row.

### `ds_delete_file`

Delete a file (data-object) or directory (collection).

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `path` (required) | string |  | The path to the file (data-object) or directory (collection) to delete. |

### `ds_delete_ticket`

Revoke an existing iRODS ticket. Issuer or admin only — the server enforces this. Anonymous callers are rejected at the tool layer.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `ticket` (required) | string |  | The ticket string to delete. |

### `ds_directory_tree`

Get a recursive tree view of files (data-objects) and directories (collections). The specified path must be an iRODS path. The output is in JSON format. The output contains all entries in the given directory (collection) path.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `path` (required) | string |  | The path to the directory (collection) to list. |
| `depth` | integer | `3` | The depth of the directory tree to list. Default value is 3. Depth must be greater than or equal to 1. Depth must not be too large, otherwise the output may be too large. Maximum value is 10. |

### `ds_download_file`

Returns how to download the full contgent of a file (data-object) with the specified path. The specified path must be an iRODS path. Returns how to download the file using WebDAV, GoCommands (gocmd), and iCommands.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `irods_path` (required) | string |  | The iRODS path to the file (data-object) to download. |
| `local_path` (required) | string |  | The local path to download the file (data-object) to. Must be a full path including the file name. |

### `ds_execute_rule`

Run an iRODS rule. Supply either rule_name (server-installed) or rule_text (inline iRL). Output parameters are returned as a dict; iRODS stdout/stderr are returned when output_parameters includes 'ruleExecOut'. Path-typed input parameters are checked against the caller's accessible paths before the rule fires.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `rule_name` | string \| null | `null` | Name of a server-installed rule to invoke. |
| `rule_text` | string \| null | `null` | Inline iRL fragment to execute. |
| `input_parameters` | object |  | Input parameters bound into the rule body. |
| `output_parameters` | array of string |  | Names of rule output parameters to return. |
| `instance_name` | string | `"irods_rule_engine_plugin-irods_rule_language-instance"` | Rule engine instance to target. |

### `ds_get_file_info`

Retrieve detailed metadata about a file or directory.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `path` (required) | string |  | The path to the file (data-object) or directory (collection). |

### `ds_get_metadata`

Fetch the full AVU metadata bundle for an iRODS path (data object or collection). Returns the resolved target type alongside the AVU list.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `path` (required) | string |  | Absolute iRODS path of the data object or collection whose metadata you want. |

### `ds_get_policy_config`

Return the configuration of a named Policy Composition Framework policy. iRODS does not expose PCF config through PRC; this is a stub that returns ``config=None`` and a ``note`` documenting the limitation.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `name` (required) | string |  | Name of the PCF policy to introspect. |

### `ds_get_rule_definition`

Return the source of a named iRODS rule. iRODS does not expose rule sources through PRC; this is a best-effort tool whose ``definition`` field is None on most servers.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `name` (required) | string |  | Name of the rule to introspect. |

### `ds_get_ticket_info`

Get information about a specific iRODS ticket, such as its ID and expiration time, in JSON format. Anonymous users are not allowed to get ticket information.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `name` (required) | string |  | The name of the iRODS ticket to get information about. |

### `ds_list_allowed_directories`

Get a list of directories (collections) that this server is allowed to access. The output also contains API names that can be requested to each directory (collection).

No input fields.

### `ds_list_avus`

List AVUs (attribute-value-unit) from a file (data-object), directory (collection), resource, or user.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `target_type` (required) | `"path"` \| `"resource"` \| `"user"` |  | The type of the target to list AVU. It can be 'path', 'resource', or 'user'. |
| `target` (required) | string |  | The target to list AVU. Path for 'path' target_type, resource name for 'resource' target_type, and user name for 'user' target_type. |

### `ds_list_directory`

Get a list of files (data-objects) and directories (collections) in a specified path. The specified path must be an iRODS path. The output is in JSON format. The output contains entries in the given directory (collection) path. Use offset and limit parameters to paginate through large directories.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `path` (required) | string |  | The path to the directory (collection) to list. |
| `offset` | integer | `0` | Number of entries to skip (for pagination). Default: 0. |
| `limit` | integer | `100` | Maximum number of entries to return (for pagination). Default: 100, max: 500. |

### `ds_list_directory_details`

Get a list of files (data-objects) and directories (collections) in a specified path with full detailed info. The specified path must be an iRODS path. The output is in JSON format. The output contains entries in the given directory (collection) path, and users or groups who can access the files (data-ojects). Files (data-objects) will also have replica information. Use offset and limit parameters to paginate through large directories.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `path` (required) | string |  | The path to the directory (collection) to list. |
| `offset` | integer | `0` | Number of entries to skip (for pagination). Default: 0. |
| `limit` | integer | `100` | Maximum number of entries to return (for pagination). Default: 100, max: 500. |

### `ds_list_policies`

List policies in effect for the Data Store. With ``project_path``, returns the MESA policy AVUs (``mesa.policy.*``) set on that project root — the policies mesa-mcp itself honours. Always includes the server-side Policy Composition Framework envelope; iRODS does not expose PCF state through PRC, so that part is a documented stub.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `project_path` | string \| null | `null` | Project root collection whose MESA policy AVUs (`mesa.policy.*`) should be listed. Omit to return only the server-side Policy Composition Framework envelope. |

### `ds_list_rules`

List iRODS rules visible to the caller. Returns a best-effort list of delayed rules; the static rule base is not exposed by PRC and the ``note`` field documents that limitation.

No input fields.

### `ds_list_tickets`

Get a list of iRODS tickets. Return information about the tickets, such as their IDs and expiration times, in JSON format. Anonymous users are not allowed to list tickets.

No input fields.

### `ds_make_directory`

Make a new directory (collection).

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `path` (required) | string |  | The path to the new directory to create. |

### `ds_modify_access`

Modify data access of a user or group to a file (data-object) or directory (collection).

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `access_level` (required) | string |  | The access level to set to the user. It can be 'own', 'delete_object', 'modify_object', 'create_object', 'delete_metadata', 'modify_metadata', 'create_metadata', 'read_object', 'read_metadata', or 'null'. For iRODS version prior to 4.3.0, only 'own', 'write', 'read', and 'null' are allowed. |
| `user_or_group` (required) | string |  | The user or group to set access. You can specify a user by 'username#zone' or a group by 'groupname#zone' to set zone. if zone is not specified, the client's zone will be used. |
| `path` (required) | string |  | The path to the file (data-object) or directory (collection) to modify access. |
| `recurse` | boolean | `false` | If set, apply the given access to all entries within the given directory (collection) recursively. |

### `ds_modify_access_inheritance`

Modify data access inheritance flag of a file or directory.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `path` (required) | string |  | The path to the directory (collection) to modify access. |
| `inherit` (required) | boolean |  | If set, access to the directory (collection) will be inherited by all child entries. |
| `recurse` | boolean | `false` | If set, apply the inheritance flag to all entries within the given directory (collection) recursively. |

### `ds_modify_ticket`

Modify restrictions on an existing iRODS ticket. Cannot change the ticket's mode — that is set at issuance time. Returns the applied restrictions. Anonymous users are not allowed to modify tickets.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `ticket` (required) | string |  | The ticket string to modify. |
| `uses` | integer \| null | `null` | New uses-allowed cap. |
| `expiry` | string \| null | `null` | New ISO-8601 expiry timestamp. |
| `write_byte_limit` | integer \| null | `null` | New write-byte limit (write tickets only). |
| `host_restriction` | string \| null | `null` | Add an allowed-host restriction. |
| `user_restriction` | string \| null | `null` | Add an allowed-user restriction. |

### `ds_move_file`

Move a file (data-object) or directory (collection) to a new location.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `old_path` (required) | string |  | The old path to the file (data-object) or directory (collection). |
| `new_path` (required) | string |  | The new, complete path to move the file (data-object) or directory (collection) to, including its new name. The path must not already exist. |

### `ds_ping`

Liveness check. Echoes back the supplied message (or 'ok') and the running mesa-mcp version. No iRODS access required.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `message` | string \| null | `null` | — |

### `ds_read_file`

Read the partial content of a file (data-object) with the specified path and offset. The specified path must be an iRODS path. If the file is too large to be displayed inline, use the WebDAV URI to access it.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `path` (required) | string |  | The path to the file (data-object) to read. |
| `offset` | integer | `0` | The offset to start reading the file from. Default is 0. |
| `length` | integer | `65536` | The maximum length of the file to read. Default value is 1048576. Length must be greater than or equal to 65536. Length must not be too large, otherwise the output may be too large. Maximum value is 1048576. |

### `ds_search_files`

Recursively search for files (data-objects) and directories (collections) matching a pattern. The specified search root path must be an iRODS path. Use unix wildcards, such as '?' and '*', for the search pattern. The matching entries are returned in JSON format.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `path` (required) | string |  | The search path, which may include wildcard patterns such as '?' and '*'. |

### `ds_search_files_by_avu`

Search for files (data-objects) and directories (collections) matching iRODS AVU (attribute-value-units) using specified attribute and value. The matching entries are returned in JSON format.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `attribute` (required) | string |  | The attribute to search for. |
| `value` (required) | string |  | The value of the attribute to search for. |

### `ds_search_metadata`

Search iRODS by AVU attribute/value/unit. More permissive than ds_search_files_by_avu: any combination of attribute, value, and unit can be supplied and you can restrict the result type to data objects, collections, or both.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `attribute` | string \| null | `null` | Match only AVUs with this attribute name. |
| `value` | string \| null | `null` | Match only AVUs with this value. |
| `unit` | string \| null | `null` | Match only AVUs with this unit (often an ontology CURIE). |
| `target` | `"data_object"` \| `"collection"` \| `"both"` | `"both"` | Restrict results to data objects, collections, or both. |

### `ds_upload_file`

Returns how to upload the full contgent of a file (data-object) to the specified path. The specified path must be an iRODS path. Returns how to upload the file using WebDAV, GoCommands (gocmd), and iCommands.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `local_path` (required) | string |  | The local path to the file (data-object) to upload. |
| `irods_path` (required) | string |  | The target iRODS path to upload the file (data-object) to. |
| `is_dir` | boolean | `false` | Set to true if uploading a directory (collection). Default is false. |

### `ds_use_ticket`

Supply an iRODS ticket to the caller's iRODS session. Subsequent operations by the same caller run with the ticket applied, and their AVU writes record the ticket id in DuckLake's via_ticket column. Other callers' sessions are unaffected.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `ticket` (required) | string |  | The ticket string to use for subsequent operations. |

### `ds_write_file`

Write the partial content to a file (data-object) with the specified path and offset. The specified path must be an iRODS path. If the file is too large to be displayed inline, use the WebDAV URI to access it.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `path` (required) | string |  | The path to the file (data-object) to write to. |
| `offset` | integer | `0` | The offset to start writing the file from. Default is 0. |
| `content` (required) | string |  | The Base64-encoded content to write to the file (data-object). Maximum size is 1048576 bytes. |

## mesa_ols_*: Ontology Lookup Service

Read-only browsing of the EMBL-EBI OLS4 API. No iRODS access and no credentials needed. Upstream OLS errors come back as an `error` field (search, hierarchy, list) or as `ToolError(code="upstream_error")`.

### `mesa_ols_generate_template`

Generate a SCHEMAS-compatible template (prefix + top-level term fields) for an ontology. This is the function that drives the esiil-portal auto-generated AVU forms.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `ontology_id` (required) | string |  | Ontology identifier to generate a template for (e.g. 'envo'). |

### `mesa_ols_get_ontology`

Fetch metadata for a single OLS ontology (term count, version, homepage, preferred prefix).

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `ontology_id` (required) | string |  | Ontology identifier, e.g. 'envo', 'go', 'chebi'. Case-insensitive. |

### `mesa_ols_get_term`

Get the full record (label, CURIE, synonyms, definition, parents/children) for a single OLS term by IRI.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `ontology_id` (required) | string |  | Ontology identifier (e.g. 'envo'). |
| `iri` (required) | string |  | Full term IRI, e.g. 'http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_00000428'. |

### `mesa_ols_get_term_hierarchy`

List the direct children of an OLS term. Use this to walk an ontology's class hierarchy one level at a time.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `ontology_id` (required) | string |  | Ontology identifier (e.g. 'envo'). |
| `iri` (required) | string |  | Full IRI of the parent term. |
| `size` | integer | `50` | Max children to return. |

### `mesa_ols_list_ontologies`

List ontologies available in the EMBL-EBI Ontology Lookup Service (OLS4), paginated. Returns 266+ ontologies (ENVO, GO, CHEBI, etc.).

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `page` | integer | `0` | Zero-indexed page number. |
| `size` | integer | `25` | Results per page (1–200). |

### `mesa_ols_search_terms`

Search OLS terms across all ontologies or scoped to one. Optionally restrict to descendants of a parent IRI (hierarchy walk).

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `query` (required) | string |  | Free-text search string. |
| `ontology_id` | string \| null | `null` | Optional ontology to restrict the search (e.g. 'envo'). |
| `descendants_of` | string \| null | `null` | Optional parent term IRI. When set together with `ontology_id`, only descendants of this term are returned (uses the v1-compat `allChildrenOf` search). |
| `size` | integer | `15` | Max results. |

## mesa_avu_*: ontology terms as AVUs

Turn an OLS term into the canonical AVU triple: attribute `<ontology_id>.<snake_case_label>`, value as supplied, unit the term's CURIE. See [Metadata workflows](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/user/examples/#tag-a-file-with-an-ontology-term).

### `mesa_avu_apply_term`

Resolve an OLS term, build the canonical AVU triple (<ontology>.<snake_label>, <value>, <CURIE>), write it to the iRODS path, and record the change in the project's DuckLake. Composite of mesa_avu_from_term + ds_add_avu, in one call.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `path` (required) | string |  | Absolute iRODS path of the data object or collection to tag. |
| `ontology_id` (required) | string |  | Ontology identifier (e.g. 'envo'). |
| `value` (required) | string |  | User-supplied AVU value. Often the term label, but free-form. |
| `iri` | string \| null | `null` | Full IRI of the OLS term. Either `iri` or `curie` is required. |
| `curie` | string \| null | `null` | CURIE of the OLS term (e.g. 'ENVO:00000428'). |
| `label` | string \| null | `null` | Optional term label. When omitted, the label is looked up via OLS so the AVU attribute can be `<ontology>.<snake_case_label>`. |

If neither `iri` nor `curie` is given, the tool searches OLS for `value` and returns an MCP input request asking the user to choose among up to 8 candidate terms. On a history-mirror failure the result carries `partial_failure` with code `ducklake_mirror_failed`.

### `mesa_avu_from_term`

Pure transformation: turn an OLS term + user value into the canonical AVU triple (attribute='<ontology>.<snake_case_label>', value=<value>, unit=<CURIE>) without writing to iRODS.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `ontology_id` (required) | string |  | Ontology identifier (e.g. 'envo'). |
| `value` (required) | string |  | User-supplied AVU value. Often the term label, but free-form. |
| `iri` | string \| null | `null` | Full IRI of the term to use. Either `iri` or `curie` must be supplied, alongside `label` if you want to skip the OLS lookup. |
| `curie` | string \| null | `null` | Term CURIE (e.g. 'ENVO:00000428') — used directly as the AVU unit. |
| `label` | string \| null | `null` | Term label. If omitted, mesa-mcp fetches it from OLS using `ontology_id` + `iri`. |

## mesa_datacite_*: DataCite descriptive metadata

DataCite 4.x records stored as `datacite.*` AVUs. Only `mesa_avu_apply_datacite` touches iRODS; template, validate and export work on the data you pass in. See [DataCite metadata](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/user/datacite/).

### `mesa_avu_apply_datacite`

Validate a DataCite 4.x record and write it to an iRODS path as AVUs (canonical and/or CyVerse-template naming), mirrored to DuckLake as one snapshot.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `target` (required) | string |  | iRODS path of the data-object or collection. |
| `record` (required) | object |  | A DataCite 4.x record (validated). |
| `naming` | string | `"both"` | canonical \| cyverse_template \| both |

Fails with `datacite_invalid` before writing anything if the record does not validate. Output: `target`, `path_target_type`, `written`, `errors`, and `partial_failure` on a history-mirror failure.

### `mesa_datacite_export`

Export DataCite AVUs as a DataCite 4.x XML (for DOI registration) or REST JSON document.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `avus` (required) | array of AvuItem |  | Canonical-naming DataCite AVUs from a path. |
| `format` | `"xml"` \| `"json"` | `"xml"` | — |

Takes AVUs, not a path: read them first with `ds_list_avus` or `ds_get_metadata`. Output: `{"format", "document"}`. Fails with `datacite_incomplete` when the AVUs do not form a valid record.

### `mesa_datacite_template`

Return the DataCite 4.x field scaffold (field, required?, repeatable?, controlled vocabulary, canonical AVU key) to drive a complete, valid record.

No input fields.

### `mesa_datacite_validate`

Validate DataCite AVUs against the 4.x kernel: report missing mandatory fields, invalid controlled-vocabulary values, and whether the record is DOI-ready.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `avus` (required) | array of AvuItem |  | The candidate DataCite AVUs to validate. |

Output: `doi_ready`, `missing_mandatory`, `errors`.

## mesa_ducklake_*: AVU history

All three need `ducklake.catalog_dsn` set and the `ducklake` extra installed; otherwise they fail with `ducklake_disabled`. They also need an authenticated caller. See [Configuration](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/user/configuration/#ducklake-avu-history-catalog) and [DuckLake integration](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/dev/ducklake-integration/).

### `mesa_ducklake_history`

Read the DuckLake AVU history for an iRODS path inside a MESA-enabled project. Without as_of, returns the change log (newest first). With as_of, returns the AVUs that were in effect at that timestamp. Optional exact-match filters on attribute and unit. Read-only.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `irods_path` (required) | string |  | Absolute iRODS path of the data object or collection whose AVU history to read. Must sit inside a MESA-enabled project. |
| `attribute` | string \| null | `null` | Only return rows whose AVU attribute equals this string exactly. |
| `unit` | string \| null | `null` | Only return rows whose AVU unit equals this string exactly. Pass an empty string to match rows with no unit. |
| `as_of` | string \| null | `null` | ISO-8601 timestamp (`2026-09-01T12:00:00Z`). When set, return the AVUs in effect at that instant instead of the change log. A timestamp with no zone is read as UTC. |
| `limit` | integer | `100` | Maximum number of rows to return. Default 100; values above 1000 are capped at 1000. |

Output: `project_id`, `count` and `rows`. Each row is a mesa-ducklake `AvuChange`: `project_id`, `snapshot_id`, `irods_path`, `target_type`, `attribute`, `value`, `unit`, `op` (`add` or `delete`), `actor`, `ts`, `source`, `via_ticket`, `rule_invocation`. Errors: `not_mesa_project`, `history_project_not_registered`, `history_failed_catalog_lookup`, `history_failed_read`, `invalid_argument` (bad `as_of`).

### `mesa_ducklake_init_project`

Enroll an iRODS collection as a MESA project. Creates the <irods_path>/.mesa/ducklake/ sub-collection (or the configured ducklake.data_collection), sets the mesa.enabled=true AVU on the project root, and registers the project in the DuckLake catalog. Idempotent — safe to re-run.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `irods_path` (required) | string |  | Absolute iRODS path of the project's root collection — the collection that will carry the `mesa.enabled=true` AVU and host the DuckLake history sub-collection (`.mesa/ducklake/` unless `ducklake.data_collection` says otherwise). |

Output: `project_id`, `irods_path`, `irods_zone`, `ducklake_path`, `created_at`, `created_by`, `status`. Errors name the failing step: `init_project_failed_root_missing`, `init_project_failed_irods_create`, `init_project_failed_avu_add`, `init_project_failed_catalog_register`, and so on.

### `mesa_ducklake_time_travel`

Return the AVUs that were in effect on an iRODS path inside a MESA-enabled project at a past timestamp, read from the project's DuckLake. Changes stamped at exactly as_of are included. Optional exact-match filters on attribute and unit. Read-only.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `irods_path` (required) | string |  | Absolute iRODS path of the data object or collection whose AVUs to read. Must sit inside a MESA-enabled project. |
| `as_of` (required) | string |  | ISO-8601 timestamp (`2026-09-01T12:00:00Z`). Returns the AVUs in effect at that instant; a change stamped at exactly this time is included. A timestamp with no zone is read as UTC. Snapshot ids are not supported. |
| `attribute` | string \| null | `null` | Only return AVUs whose attribute equals this string exactly. |
| `unit` | string \| null | `null` | Only return AVUs whose unit equals this string exactly. Pass an empty string to match AVUs with no unit. |
| `limit` | integer | `100` | Maximum number of AVUs to return. Default 100; values above 1000 are capped at 1000. |

Output: `project_id`, `as_of` (normalized, UTC), `count` and `rows` (`AvuChange` records, sorted by attribute, value, unit). A bare integer `as_of` is refused: snapshot ids are not supported. Errors: `not_mesa_project`, `time_travel_project_not_registered`, `time_travel_failed_catalog_lookup`, `time_travel_failed_read`, `invalid_argument`.

## mesa_policy_*: MESA project policies

Toggle a MESA-defined policy on a project root by adding or removing the `mesa.policy.<name>=true` AVU. They do not change the iRODS server's own policy configuration. The change is mirrored to the AVU history when the root is MESA-enabled; a mirror failure is ignored.

### `mesa_policy_disable`

Disable a MESA policy on a project root collection by removing the ``mesa.policy.<policy_name>`` AVU. Records the change into the project's DuckLake when MESA-enabled.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `project_path` (required) | string |  | iRODS path of the project root collection. |
| `policy_name` (required) | string |  | Short policy identifier (becomes the suffix of the `mesa.policy.<name>` AVU). |

### `mesa_policy_enable`

Enable a MESA policy on a project root collection by writing the ``mesa.policy.<policy_name>=true`` AVU. Records the change into the project's DuckLake when MESA-enabled.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `project_path` (required) | string |  | iRODS path of the project root collection. |
| `policy_name` (required) | string |  | Short policy identifier (becomes the suffix of the `mesa.policy.<name>` AVU). |

- [Adding tools](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/dev/adding-tools/)

# Metadata workflows

What this page covers: end-to-end sequences of mesa-mcp tool calls for
the metadata tasks people ask about most. Each call is written as
`{"tool": …, "input": …}`; your MCP client sends the same JSON whatever
its syntax. For every field of every tool, see the
[Tools reference](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/user/tools-reference/). For DataCite records, see
[DataCite metadata](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/user/datacite/).

## Before you start

- An **AVU** is an iRODS metadata triple: attribute, value, unit. Data
  objects (files) and collections (folders) can carry any number of them.
- Every tool that takes a path checks it against your **accessible
  paths**: your home collection (`/<zone>/home/<user>`) and the shared
  tree (`/<zone>/home/shared`). Anything else fails with `forbidden`.
- The `anonymous` user (no credentials) gets only the shared tree, and
  iRODS gives it read-only access. Writes and tickets need a real CyVerse
  account. See [Configuration](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/user/configuration/#how-credentials-are-resolved).

## Find files by AVU

Two search tools query the iRODS catalog (iCAT). Both return data objects
and collections, and both drop any hit outside your accessible paths.

**Exact attribute and value**, the shape `irods-mcp-server` uses:

```json
{"tool": "ds_search_files_by_avu",
 "input": {"attribute": "envo.biome", "value": "tropical moist broadleaf forest"}}
```

The result lists `matching_entries`, each with `path`, `entry_type`
(`data_object` or `collection`) and `name`.

**Any combination of attribute, value and unit**, with a type filter:

```json
{"tool": "ds_search_metadata",
 "input": {"unit": "ENVO:00000428", "target": "data_object"}}
```

Each of `attribute`, `value` and `unit` is an exact match; at least one is
required. `target` is `data_object`, `collection` or `both` (the default).
Searching by `unit` finds every AVU tagged with one ontology term,
whatever value was typed.

**Find MESA-enabled projects** by searching for the project marker:

```json
{"tool": "ds_search_files_by_avu", "input": {"attribute": "mesa.enabled", "value": "true"}}
```

To read what is on one path, use `ds_list_avus` (`target_type: "path"`;
it also handles `resource` and `user`) or `ds_get_metadata`, which
resolves whether the path is a data object or collection and returns its
AVUs. Each AVU comes back with `id`, `attribute`, `value` and `unit`.

## Tag a file with an ontology term

mesa-mcp browses the [EMBL-EBI Ontology Lookup Service](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/)
(OLS4) and writes the chosen term as an AVU of a fixed shape:

| AVU field | Content | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `attribute` | `<ontology_id>.<snake_case term label>`, ontology id lowercased | `envo.biome` |
| `value` | Free text the user supplies (often a label, but not checked) | `tropical moist broadleaf forest` |
| `unit` | The term's **CURIE** | `ENVO:00000428` |

The term's IRI is not stored in the AVU. The `unit` slot holding a CURIE
is what marks an AVU as ontology-sourced. This is the same shape
`cyverse/esiil-portal` writes, so AVUs written by the portal and by
mesa-mcp are interchangeable. The label is converted by
`_label_to_snake` in `ols/client.py`: non-alphanumeric characters are
removed, whitespace becomes `_`, and the result is lowercased (`pH value`
becomes `ph_value`).

### 1. Find the term

```json
{"tool": "mesa_ols_search_terms", "input": {"query": "biome", "ontology_id": "envo", "size": 5}}
```

The result is `{"results": [...], "count": n}`; each hit has `label`,
`curie`, `iri` and `ontologyId`. Other browsing tools:

- `mesa_ols_list_ontologies` (`page` from 0, `size` up to 200) lists the
  OLS catalog.
- `mesa_ols_get_term` (`ontology_id`, `iri`) returns the full record:
  definition, synonyms, parents and children.
- `mesa_ols_get_term_hierarchy` (`ontology_id`, `iri`, `size` default 50)
  lists a term's direct children, so you can walk down one level at a
  time. `mesa_ols_search_terms` with `descendants_of` (and `ontology_id`)
  searches within a branch.

### 2. Preview the AVU (optional)

`mesa_avu_from_term` builds the triple without writing anything:

```json
{"tool": "mesa_avu_from_term",
 "input": {"ontology_id": "envo",
           "iri": "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_00000428",
           "value": "tropical moist broadleaf forest"}}
```

```json
{"avu": {"attribute": "envo.biome",
         "value": "tropical moist broadleaf forest",
         "unit": "ENVO:00000428"},
 "term": {"ontologyId": "envo", "label": "biome",
          "curie": "ENVO:00000428",
          "iri": "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_00000428"}}
```

With an `iri`, the label and CURIE are looked up in OLS. With only a
`curie`, you must also pass `label`.

### 3. Write it

`mesa_avu_apply_term` takes the same inputs plus `path`, writes the AVU
through the same code as `ds_add_avu`, and mirrors it to the project's
AVU history:

```json
{"tool": "mesa_avu_apply_term",
 "input": {"path": "/iplant/home/alice/proj/plot7.csv",
           "ontology_id": "envo",
           "iri": "http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_00000428",
           "value": "tropical moist broadleaf forest"}}
```

If you give neither `iri` nor `curie`, the tool searches OLS for `value`
in that ontology and, instead of failing, returns an **input request**
(MCP 2026-07-28 multi-round-trip) asking the user to pick one of up to 8
candidate terms. The client sends the choice back in a follow-up call and
the write goes ahead. A choice that was not among the offered candidates
is refused. If OLS finds nothing, the tool fails with `invalid_argument`.

### Template forms

`mesa_ols_generate_template` (`ontology_id`) returns an ontology's
top-level terms as a form template. It is the function behind
esiil-portal's auto-generated metadata forms.

## Add several AVUs at once

`ds_add_avus` writes many AVUs to one path in one call and records them as
a single history snapshot:

```json
{"tool": "ds_add_avus",
 "input": {"target": "/iplant/home/alice/proj/plot7.csv",
           "avus": [{"attribute": "site", "value": "plot 7"},
                    {"attribute": "envo.biome", "value": "tropical moist broadleaf forest",
                     "unit": "ENVO:00000428"}]}}
```

## Enroll a project for history

AVU history is kept only for paths inside a **MESA-enabled project**: a
collection carrying `mesa.enabled=true`. Enroll one once:

```json
{"tool": "mesa_ducklake_init_project", "input": {"irods_path": "/iplant/home/alice/proj"}}
```

It creates `/iplant/home/alice/proj/.mesa/ducklake/`, where the history's
Parquet files live, sets `mesa.enabled=true` on the root, and registers
the project in the catalog. It is safe to re-run. From then on, every AVU
written through `ds_add_avu`, `ds_add_avus`, `ds_delete_avu`,
`mesa_avu_apply_term`, `mesa_avu_apply_datacite`, `mesa_policy_enable` or
`mesa_policy_disable` under that root is recorded. The server needs
`ducklake.catalog_dsn` and the `ducklake` extra; otherwise the history
tools fail with `ducklake_disabled`.

## See how metadata changed

**The change log for a path**, newest first:

```json
{"tool": "mesa_ducklake_history",
 "input": {"irods_path": "/iplant/home/alice/proj/plot7.csv", "attribute": "envo.biome"}}
```

The result is `{"project_id", "count", "rows"}`. Each row is one AVU
change: `snapshot_id`, `irods_path`, `target_type`, `attribute`, `value`,
`unit`, `op` (`add` or `delete`), `actor` (the iRODS user), `ts`,
`source` (for example `mesa-mcp:mesa_avu_apply_term`), `via_ticket` and
`rule_invocation`. `attribute` and `unit` are optional exact-match filters
(pass `unit: ""` for AVUs with no unit). `limit` defaults to 100 and is
capped at 1000.

**The AVUs a path had at a past instant** (time travel):

```json
{"tool": "mesa_ducklake_time_travel",
 "input": {"irods_path": "/iplant/home/alice/proj/plot7.csv",
           "as_of": "2026-09-01T12:00:00Z"}}
```

`as_of` is required and must be an ISO-8601 timestamp. A timestamp with no
zone is read as UTC. A change stamped exactly at `as_of` is included (the
library reads rows with `ts <= as_of`). **Snapshot ids are not supported**:
a bare number is refused with `invalid_argument`. The result adds the
normalized `as_of` and sorts the AVUs by attribute, value and unit.
`mesa_ducklake_history` with `as_of` returns the same set without the
sorting.

Errors you may see: `not_mesa_project` (no ancestor carries
`mesa.enabled=true`), `history_project_not_registered` or
`time_travel_project_not_registered` (the marker is there but the catalog
has no row; run `mesa_ducklake_init_project`), and `ducklake_disabled`.

There is no MCP tool for diffing two snapshots or listing snapshots; see
[DuckLake integration](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/dev/ducklake-integration/#mcp-tools-versus-the-python-api).

## Share access with a ticket

An iRODS ticket is a token that grants read or write access to one path.
mesa-mcp manages the whole lifecycle. **Anonymous users cannot create,
use, modify, list or inspect tickets.**

```text
ds_create_ticket    path, mode ("read" | "write"), optional uses_allowed, expiry (ISO-8601),
                    write_byte_limit, host_restriction, user_restriction -> ticket string
ds_use_ticket       ticket -> binds it to your own pooled iRODS session
  ...               later calls run with the ticket applied
ds_modify_ticket    ticket, new uses / expiry / limits (the mode cannot change)
ds_list_tickets     list tickets
ds_get_ticket_info  name -> one ticket's details
ds_delete_ticket    ticket -> revoke (issuer or admin, enforced by iRODS)
```

`ds_use_ticket` attaches the ticket to the session mesa-mcp keeps for your
identity, so it applies to your later calls and never to another
caller's. Every AVU write you make on that session is recorded in the
history with the ticket id in the **`via_ticket`** column, so an auditor
can see which changes came through shared credentials. Creating or
modifying a ticket is not itself recorded in the history. Binding a
ticket does not widen mesa-mcp's own path check: paths must still be in
your home or shared tree.

## See also

- [Tools reference](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/user/tools-reference/)
- [DataCite metadata](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/user/datacite/)
- [DuckLake integration](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/dev/ducklake-integration/) for how writes are
  mirrored.
- [OLS internals](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/dev/ols-internals/) for the AVU contract with
  esiil-portal.

# DataCite metadata

What this page covers: how to record a dataset's descriptive metadata in
the [DataCite 4.x](https://schema.datacite.org/meta/kernel-4/) kernel as
iRODS AVUs, check that the record is complete enough for a DOI, and export
it as DataCite XML or JSON. Four tools do this; they never call DataCite
itself and do not register DOIs.

| Tool | Reads or writes iRODS? | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mesa_datacite_template` | No | Returns the field scaffold: each field, whether it is mandatory or repeatable, its controlled vocabulary, and its canonical AVU key. |
| `mesa_avu_apply_datacite` | Writes | Validates a DataCite record and writes it to a path as AVUs, then mirrors all of them to the AVU history as one snapshot. |
| `mesa_datacite_validate` | No | Checks a list of AVUs for the mandatory fields and valid vocabulary values; reports `doi_ready`. |
| `mesa_datacite_export` | No | Rebuilds the record from a list of AVUs and returns DataCite kernel-4 XML or DataCite REST JSON. |

## AVU naming

DataCite AVUs always have an empty `unit`. Two naming schemes exist.

**Canonical** (what export and validate read):

- Scalars are `datacite.<field>`: `datacite.identifier`,
  `datacite.identifierType`, `datacite.publisher`,
  `datacite.publicationYear`, `datacite.resourceTypeGeneral`,
  `datacite.resourceType`, `datacite.language`, `datacite.version`.
- Repeatable or structured fields are indexed from 1 with sub-fields:
  `datacite.title.1.value`, `datacite.creator.1.name`,
  `datacite.creator.1.affiliation`, `datacite.creator.1.nameIdentifier`,
  `datacite.subject.1.value`, `datacite.relatedIdentifier.1.relationType`,
  `datacite.format.1`, `datacite.size.1`, and so on. The index keeps a
  creator's name, affiliation and ORCID together, which flat AVUs cannot.

**CyVerse template** (the column names of CyVerse's DOI-request
template): `datacite.title`, `datacite.creator`, `datacite.publisher`,
`datacite.publicationyear`, `datacite.resourcetype`, `Identifier`,
`identifierType`, `creatorAffiliation`, `ResourceType`, `Subject`,
`Rights`, `Description`, and similar. Only the first title, creator,
rights and description are written in this form. `LEGACY_CROSSWALK` in
`src/mesa_mcp/datacite/schema.py` maps these names to kernel fields.

`mesa_avu_apply_datacite` takes `naming` = `canonical`,
`cyverse_template` or `both` (the default). `both` writes the union,
skipping duplicate attribute/value pairs.

## Mandatory fields

A record is DOI-ready when it has all six kernel fields: `identifier`,
`title`, `creator`, `publisher`, `publicationYear` (a 4-digit year) and
`resourceTypeGeneral` (one of DataCite's controlled values, such as
`Dataset`). Call `mesa_datacite_template` to get the vocabularies for
`resourceTypeGeneral`, `contributorType`, `descriptionType` and
`relationType`.

## Write a record

```json
{
  "tool": "mesa_avu_apply_datacite",
  "input": {
    "target": "/iplant/home/alice/proj/leaf-images",
    "naming": "canonical",
    "record": {
      "identifier": "10.1234/example",
      "titles": ["Leaf phenotype images, 2026 field season"],
      "creators": [{"name": "Doe, Jane", "affiliation": "Example University"}],
      "publisher": "CyVerse Data Commons",
      "publicationYear": 2026,
      "resourceTypeGeneral": "Dataset"
    }
  }
}
```

The record is validated before anything is written. A bad record fails
with `datacite_invalid` and the Pydantic errors in `details`. On success
the result reports `written` (the count), any per-AVU `errors`, and a
`partial_failure` with code `ducklake_mirror_failed` if the history mirror
failed after the iRODS writes. The path must be inside your accessible
paths (home or shared).

## Check and export a record

`mesa_datacite_validate` and `mesa_datacite_export` take a list of AVUs,
**not a path**. They do not read iRODS. To export what is on a dataset:

1. Read the AVUs with `ds_list_avus` (`target_type: "path"`) or
   `ds_get_metadata`.
2. Pass on the `datacite.*` AVUs. The record is rebuilt from the
   canonical names, so a path written with `naming: "canonical"` or
   `"both"` exports; one written only with `cyverse_template` names does
   not.
3. Check completeness:

    ```json
    {"tool": "mesa_datacite_validate", "input": {"avus": [ … ]}}
    ```

    The result is `{"doi_ready": true|false, "missing_mandatory": [...],
    "errors": [...]}`.

4. Export:

    ```json
    {"tool": "mesa_datacite_export", "input": {"avus": [ … ], "format": "xml"}}
    ```

    `format` is `xml` (the default; DataCite kernel-4 XML, namespace
    `http://datacite.org/schema/kernel-4`, the form a DOI registration
    takes) or `json` (DataCite REST JSON). The result is
    `{"format": …, "document": "<string>"}`. AVUs that cannot form a valid
    record fail with `datacite_incomplete`.

Submitting the XML to DataCite, or to CyVerse's DOI request process, is
outside mesa-mcp.

## History

Because `mesa_avu_apply_datacite` writes one snapshot per record, a
record's history in a MESA-enabled project can be read with
`mesa_ducklake_history`, filtered by attribute (for example
`attribute: "datacite.publisher"`). See
[Metadata workflows](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/user/examples/#see-how-metadata-changed).

## See also

- [Tools reference](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/user/tools-reference/#mesa_datacite_-datacite-descriptive-metadata)
- [DataCite support design record](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/design/2026-06-08-datacite-support-design/)
  for why the scheme looks like this.

# Architecture

What this page covers: how mesa-mcp is structured at runtime, from the
CLI entry point to tool dispatch, and the subsystems behind the tools. For
goals and recorded design decisions, read
[CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/idss-mesa/mesa-mcp/blob/main/CLAUDE.md).

## Process layout

```
mesa-mcp (console script -> mesa_mcp.__main__:main)
  │
  ├─ __main__.py   argparse: --config, --transport, --log-level, --version
  ├─ config.py     load_config(): flag > env > YAML > defaults; set_active_config()
  ├─ logging.py    structlog setup
  └─ server.py     run(config) -> MesaServer(config).serve(transport)
                     │  __post_init__: load_plugins(), snapshot the tool registry
                     ├─ stdio: resolve_credentials() once, bind contextvars,
                     │         mcp.server.Server over stdio
                     └─ sse:   Starlette app under uvicorn (transport/sse.py)
                               /sse + /messages/ (old SSE), /mcp (Streamable HTTP),
                               /healthz, /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource
```

The server targets the **MCP 2026-07-28** specification through the `mcp`
Python SDK 2.x (`mcp>=2.0,<3`). Registration uses SDK 2.x constructor
callbacks (`on_list_tools`, `on_call_tool`); the 1.x decorator API is not
used.

## Package map

| Package / module | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `server.py` | Tool registry (`register_tool`, `ToolSpec`), plugin loader, `_invoke_handler`, `MesaServer`, `ds_ping`. |
| `config.py` | Pydantic config model (`irods`, `ols`, `ducklake`, `server`) and loader. |
| `context.py` | Contextvars for the current `AuthValue`, config, client pool and ticket; session-ticket binding. |
| `errors.py` | `ToolError` (structured failure) and `InputRequired` (multi-round-trip question). |
| `auth/` | `AuthValue` model, credential resolution (`extract.py`, `irods_env.py`), `iRODSAccount` building, Keycloak claims. |
| `transport/` | HTTP app (`sse.py`), Streamable HTTP manager, OIDC verifier, `/healthz`, RFC 9728 metadata. |
| `irods/` | Session pool, path checks (`access.py`), AVU/ticket/rule/policy helpers, WebDAV URL minting, and `tools/` (one module per `ds_*` tool). |
| `ols/` | `OLSClient` (ported from esiil-portal), AVU transforms, and `tools/` (`mesa_ols_*`, `mesa_avu_from_term`, `mesa_avu_apply_term`, `mesa_policy_*`). |
| `datacite/` | DataCite 4.x schema, AVU transform, XML/JSON export, and `tools/`. |
| `ducklake/` | Facade over mesa-ducklake (`client.py`) and `tools/` (`mesa_ducklake_*`). |

## Tool registry

Each tool module decorates an async handler with `@register_tool(name,
description, input_model=..., output_model=..., meta=...)`, which stores a
`ToolSpec` in the module-level `_REGISTRY` dict. A duplicate name raises
`ValueError` at import time.

Registration happens by import side effect. At the bottom of `server.py`,
`mesa_mcp.datacite.tools`, `mesa_mcp.ols`, `mesa_mcp.ducklake.tools` and
`mesa_mcp.irods.tools` are imported. Each `tools/__init__.py` walks its
directory with `pkgutil.iter_modules` and imports every module whose name
does not start with `_`. Importing `mesa_mcp.server` therefore registers
all 52 built-in tools.

Third-party packages add tools through the **`mesa_mcp.tools` entry-point
group**. `MesaServer.__post_init__` calls `load_plugins()`, which imports
each entry point once. A plugin that fails to import is skipped with a
warning unless `server.strict_plugins` is true. A plugin can set its own
surface family with `meta={"io.mesa/surface": "<family>"}`.

`MesaServer._tool_definitions()` turns each `ToolSpec` into an MCP `Tool`:
the input model's JSON Schema with an explicit `$schema` of JSON Schema
2020-12, an `outputSchema` when `output_model` is set (only `ds_ping`
today), and `_meta["io.mesa/surface"]` (`irods`, `ontology`, `datacite`,
`history`, `policy`, `croissant`, or the plugin's own). `tools/list` is
served with a 5-minute public cache hint.

## Dispatch

1. The SDK's `on_call_tool` callback calls `MesaServer.call(name,
   arguments)`.
2. `_invoke_handler` validates the arguments against `input_model`
   (failure becomes `ToolError(code="invalid_argument")`).
3. Handlers that declare an `auth_value` keyword get the current caller's
   `AuthValue` from the contextvar. Handlers that declare `elicited` get
   the user's answer on a multi-round-trip follow-up.
4. The handler's `dict` result is returned as `structuredContent` and as
   one JSON text block. A non-dict result is an `internal_error`.
5. A `ToolError` becomes `{"error": {code, message, details}}` with
   `isError: true`. An `InputRequired` becomes an MCP `InputRequiredResult`
   carrying a form schema and a base64 `requestState` (at most 16 KiB),
   which the client returns on the follow-up. `mesa_avu_apply_term` uses
   this to ask the user to choose an ontology term.

## Transports

**stdio** (default). One user per process. `resolve_credentials()` picks
the identity once at startup (explicit settings, then `~/.irods`, then
anonymous; see [Configuration](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/user/configuration/#how-credentials-are-resolved)),
binds it into the contextvars, and runs the SDK loop. Clients on either
the legacy handshake or the 2026-07-28 per-request era work.

**HTTP** (`--transport sse`). A Starlette app under uvicorn, bound to
`server.bind_address:bind_port`:

- `GET /sse` and `POST /messages/`: the older SSE transport, used by
  `mcp-remote` bridges.
- `/mcp`: Streamable HTTP, used by claude.ai custom connectors.
- `GET /healthz`: unauthenticated liveness, `{"status": "ok", "version"}`.
- `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`: RFC 9728 metadata pointing
  at CyVerse Keycloak.

Every other route requires a CyVerse Keycloak bearer JWT, checked by
`OIDCAuthenticator` (signature against the realm JWKS, `exp`, `iss`, and
`aud` unless `oidc_require_audience` is false). With no
`oidc_discovery_url` set, requests are let through without authentication
for local development. Operator details are in
[HTTP / SSE transport](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/deploy/http-sse/) and [OIDC](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/deploy/oidc/).

## Authentication and path safety

- `AuthValue` (`auth/models.py`) is a frozen model of the caller:
  username, zone, password (`repr=False`), auth scheme (`native`, `pam`
  or `anonymous`), proxy user, ticket, home and shared paths.
- `accessible_paths()` returns the caller's home collection plus the
  shared tree; anonymous callers get only the shared tree. A ticket does
  not add a path today.
- `irods.access.assert_allowed(path, auth_value)` normalizes the path
  (collapses `//`, resolves `..`, strips a trailing slash) and raises
  `ToolError(code="forbidden")` for anything outside those paths. Every
  path-taking tool calls it before touching iRODS and uses the returned
  path.

## iRODS

`irods.client_pool.IRODSClientPool` keeps one `python-irodsclient`
`iRODSSession` per caller identity, keyed by `AuthValue.cache_key()` (a
SHA-256 digest), with LRU eviction at 32 entries. `ds_use_ticket` supplies
a ticket to the caller's pooled session and records it as a session
attribute, which is how `via_ticket` survives across calls. The `ds_*`
tools copy their names and input shapes from
[cyverse/irods-mcp-server](https://github.com/cyverse/irods-mcp-server);
see [Porting from Go](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/dev/porting-from-go/).

Some tools are limited by what `python-irodsclient` exposes:
`ds_list_policies` and `ds_get_policy_config` return a documented stub
with a `note`, `ds_get_rule_definition` usually returns no definition, and
`ds_list_rules` lists delayed rules only.

## OLS

`ols.client.OLSClient` wraps the public OLS4 API with seven in-process TTL
caches and two retries on 429/502/503/504. Tools get a process-wide
instance from `mesa_mcp.ols.get_default_client()`. `ols/transform.py`
holds the AVU transforms shared with esiil-portal. See
[OLS internals](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/dev/ols-internals/).

## DataCite

`datacite/schema.py` is the DataCite 4.x kernel as Pydantic models and
enums; `transform.py` converts records to and from `datacite.*` AVUs;
`export.py` writes kernel-4 XML and REST JSON. No network calls. See
[DataCite metadata](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/user/datacite/).

## DuckLake

`ducklake/client.py` is the only place mesa-mcp touches mesa-ducklake. It
builds one `DuckLakeClient` lazily from config and exposes
`record_avu_change` / `record_avu_changes`, which AVU-writing tools call
after a successful iRODS write. mesa-ducklake is the optional `ducklake`
extra; without it, or without `ducklake.catalog_dsn`, mirroring is a
no-op. See [DuckLake integration](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/dev/ducklake-integration/).

## Dependencies

From `pyproject.toml`:

| Package | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `mcp>=2.0,<3` | MCP SDK (2026-07-28 spec). |
| `python-irodsclient>=2.0` | iRODS client. |
| `pydantic>=2.6` | Config and tool input models. |
| `pyyaml` | YAML config. |
| `requests`, `cachetools` | OLS HTTP calls and TTL caches. |
| `structlog` | Logging. |
| `pyjwt[crypto]>=2.10`, `httpx>=0.28` | OIDC token verification, discovery and JWKS fetches. |
| `uvicorn>=0.30`, `starlette>=0.40` | HTTP transport. |

Extras: `ducklake` (`mesa-ducklake>=0.2`), `croissant`
(`mesa-croissant>=1.3`), and `dev` (`pytest`, `pytest-asyncio`,
`pytest-mock`, `ruff`, `mypy`, type stubs). Neither mesa-ducklake nor
mesa-croissant is on PyPI.

## Error contract

Handlers raise `ToolError(code, message, details)` for anything a client
should see. Python tracebacks never reach the client. Codes are short and
stable (`invalid_argument`, `forbidden`, `not_found`, `irods_error`,
`upstream_error`, `ducklake_disabled`, and per-tool codes such as
`init_project_failed_root_missing`). An AVU write whose history mirror
fails still succeeds and reports `partial_failure`.

## See also

- [DuckLake integration](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/dev/ducklake-integration/)
- [Adding tools](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/dev/adding-tools/)
- [Testing](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/dev/testing/)

# DuckLake integration

What this page covers: how mesa-mcp talks to
[mesa-ducklake](https://github.com/idss-mesa/mesa-ducklake), the library
that keeps the AVU (attribute, value, unit) history of every file and
folder in a MESA-enabled project. It explains why the library runs
in-process, the exact path an AVU write takes into the history, and which
history operations an agent can call.

## In-process, behind one facade

mesa-ducklake is a Python package. mesa-mcp imports it **in-process**: the
`DuckLakeClient` and its DuckDB connections live inside the mesa-mcp
process. There is no separate history service and no socket.

This is decision 3 in the repository's
[CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/idss-mesa/mesa-mcp/blob/main/CLAUDE.md)
("mesa-ducklake API surface: Python import, in-process"). The reasons it
records are:

- mesa-ducklake ships as a Python package, so importing it is the direct
  route.
- The import surface stays narrow, a single facade in
  [`src/mesa_mcp/ducklake/client.py`](https://github.com/idss-mesa/mesa-mcp/blob/main/src/mesa_mcp/ducklake/client.py),
  so the two repositories can evolve independently and a future
  **out-of-process** split stays cheap.

No other rationale (latency, transactions) is recorded. The facade
imports `mesa_ducklake` lazily inside its functions; the only other
import is `mesa_ducklake.time_travel.parse_as_of` in the time-travel
tool, also lazy, with a local fallback. These are the facade's entry
points:

| Facade entry point | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `get_default_client()` | Returns the process-wide `mesa_ducklake.DuckLakeClient`, built lazily on first use from `ducklake.catalog_dsn`, `cache_dir`, `cache_cap_bytes` and `data_collection`. Returns `None` when DuckLake is disabled. |
| `record_avu_change(...)` | Mirrors one AVU add or delete for one path. Called by write tools after the iRODS write succeeds. |
| `record_avu_changes(...)` | Mirrors many AVU changes for one path as a **single** snapshot. |
| `ducklake_subpath(root, data_collection)` | Computes `<root>/.mesa/ducklake` (or the configured sub-collection) without importing mesa-ducklake. |

### Optional dependency

mesa-ducklake is the optional `ducklake` extra (`pip install
"mesa-mcp[ducklake]"`, version 0.2 or newer, which needs DuckDB 2.0). It is
not on PyPI, so install it from its checkout first. `get_default_client()`
returns `None`, and mirroring becomes a silent no-op, when either:

- `ducklake.catalog_dsn` (`MESA_MCP_DUCKLAKE__CATALOG_DSN`) is empty, or
- `import mesa_ducklake` fails (a warning `mesa_ducklake_unavailable` is
  logged once).

AVU writes still succeed in iRODS in both cases; they are just not
recorded. The three `mesa_ducklake_*` tools refuse to run instead, with
error code `ducklake_disabled`.

The DSN picks the catalog backend inside mesa-ducklake: `postgresql://…`
(hosted, several writers), `duckdb:///abs/path.duckdb` (one local
process), or `quack://host:port` (a DuckDB file shared through
`mesa-ducklake serve-catalog`). See [Configuration](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/user/configuration/#ducklake-avu-history-catalog).

## What makes a project MESA-enabled

A collection is a MESA project when it carries the AVU
`mesa.enabled=true`. `mesa_ducklake_init_project` sets that up in four
idempotent steps:

1. Check the root exists and is a collection.
2. Create `<root>/.mesa/ducklake/` (or `<root>/<ducklake.data_collection>`).
3. Add `mesa.enabled=true` to the root if it is not already there.
4. Find or register the project in the catalog
   (`DuckLakeClient.find_project_by_path` / `register_project`).

Each step fails with its own code (`init_project_failed_root_missing`,
`init_project_failed_irods_create`, `init_project_failed_avu_add`,
`init_project_failed_catalog_register`, and so on). The tool does not
change ACLs on the new sub-collection.

Detection reads only the AVU. The facade walks the path and each parent up
to `/`, and returns the first collection whose `mesa.enabled` value is
`true`, `yes` or `1`. Results are cached per `(zone, collection)` for 5
minutes, so an admin flipping the marker takes up to 5 minutes to be seen.

## How an AVU write reaches the history

These tools mirror their writes:

| Tool | Mirror call | Snapshots per call |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ds_add_avu` | `record_avu_change(op="add")` | 1 |
| `ds_delete_avu` | `record_avu_change(op="delete")` | 1 |
| `ds_add_avus` | `record_avu_changes` | 1 for the whole batch |
| `mesa_avu_apply_term` | `record_avu_change(op="add")` | 1 |
| `mesa_avu_apply_datacite` | `record_avu_changes` | 1 for the whole record |
| `mesa_policy_enable` / `mesa_policy_disable` | `record_avu_change` on `mesa.policy.<name>` | 1 |

The sequence for one write:

1. The tool checks the path with `assert_allowed` and writes the AVU to
   iRODS through `python-irodsclient`.
2. **Only after that succeeds**, it calls `record_avu_change` with the
   caller's `AuthValue`, the normalized path, `target_type`
   (`data_object` or `collection`), the triple, `op` and its own tool name.
3. The facade returns early (no-op) if DuckLake is disabled, if no iRODS
   session was passed, or if no ancestor carries `mesa.enabled=true`.
4. It looks up the project with `find_project_by_path(project_root)`. If
   the marker is present but the catalog has no row, the write path
   **registers the project** on the spot. (The read tools do not; they
   fail with `*_project_not_registered`.)
5. It builds a `mesa_ducklake.models.AvuChange`:
   - `actor` = the iRODS username,
   - `source` = `"mesa-mcp:<tool name>"`, for example
     `mesa-mcp:mesa_avu_apply_term`,
   - `via_ticket` = the ticket bound to this caller's session by
     `ds_use_ticket` (the `mesa.via_ticket` session attribute), else
     `None`.
6. It calls `DuckLakeClient.record_changes(project_id, actor, changes,
   note, session=session)`. mesa-ducklake then runs its own
   push-before-commit protocol: it writes one Parquet file, pushes it to
   `<project>/.mesa/ducklake/` in iRODS, and commits the snapshot row.

Only **path** targets are mirrored. `ds_add_avu` and `ds_delete_avu` also
accept `target_type` `resource` or `user`; those AVUs go to iRODS but not
to the history, because the history is per project and a resource or user
is not inside one.

### When the mirror fails

The iRODS change is not rolled back. The facade raises
`DuckLakeMirrorError`, and the tool returns its normal result plus:

```json
"partial_failure": {
  "code": "ducklake_mirror_failed",
  "message": "DuckLake write failed for project …",
  "project_id": "…"
}
```

`mesa_policy_enable` and `mesa_policy_disable` are the exception: they
treat the mirror as best-effort and drop the error.

### What is not mirrored

- AVUs on resources and users (see above).
- AVU changes made outside mesa-mcp (`imeta`, other clients) unless the
  iRODS rule callbacks from mesa-ducklake's `irods-rules/` are installed on
  the server. mesa-mcp has no part in that path.
- Ticket creation and modification. `ds_create_ticket` and
  `ds_modify_ticket` do not write to the history; only AVU writes made
  *through* a ticket carry `via_ticket`.

## Reading the history

Two read-only tools use the same project lookup. Both require an
authenticated caller and a path inside a registered MESA project.

| Tool | mesa-ducklake call | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mesa_ducklake_history` | `get_history`, or `get_avus_as_of` when `as_of` is set | The change log for a path, newest first, or the AVUs in effect at `as_of` |
| `mesa_ducklake_time_travel` | `get_avus_as_of` (`as_of` required) | The AVUs in effect at `as_of`, sorted by attribute, value, unit |

Rows are `AvuChange` records: `project_id`, `snapshot_id`, `irods_path`,
`target_type`, `attribute`, `value`, `unit`, `op`, `actor`, `ts`,
`source`, `via_ticket`, `rule_invocation`. The `attribute` and `unit`
filters are exact matches applied in mesa-mcp after the read, because
mesa-ducklake has no filter arguments. `limit` defaults to 100 and is
capped at 1000. `as_of` is an ISO-8601 timestamp; a timestamp without a
zone is read as UTC, and a bare integer (a snapshot id) is refused with
`invalid_argument`.

## MCP tools versus the Python API

An agent can call three history tools:

- `mesa_ducklake_init_project`
- `mesa_ducklake_history`
- `mesa_ducklake_time_travel`

Everything else on `mesa_ducklake.DuckLakeClient` is **Python API only**.
A program that imports mesa-ducklake can call it; an MCP client cannot:

| `DuckLakeClient` method | Exposed as an MCP tool? |
| --- | --- |
| `register_project`, `find_project_by_path` | Indirectly, through `mesa_ducklake_init_project` and the write mirror |
| `record_changes` | Indirectly, through the write tools listed above |
| `get_history`, `get_avus_as_of` | Yes, through `mesa_ducklake_history` and `mesa_ducklake_time_travel` |
| `get_avus` (current state from the history) | No. Use `ds_list_avus` for the live iRODS state. |
| `get_project` | No |
| `list_snapshots` | No |
| `diff` (between two snapshot ids) | No |
| `recover_pending_pushes` | No. Use the `mesa-ducklake recover` CLI. |

`mesa_ducklake_snapshot` and `mesa_ducklake_diff` appear in the tool plan
in CLAUDE.md but are **not registered**. The back-compat stub class
`mesa_mcp.ducklake.client.DuckLakeClient` still has `snapshot` and `diff`
methods; they raise `NotImplementedError` and point you at
`get_default_client()`.

## Tests

`tests/test_ducklake_client.py`, `test_ducklake_init_project.py`,
`test_ducklake_history.py` and `test_ducklake_time_travel.py` inject a fake
client with `set_default_client(...)`, so they run without mesa-ducklake.
`tests/test_config_active.py` exercises the real library and skips when the
extra is missing; CI's `ducklake-integration` job installs it and fails if
those tests skip. See [Testing](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/dev/testing/).

## See also

- [Architecture](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/dev/architecture/)
- [Metadata workflows](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/user/examples/) for the history tools from a
  user's point of view.
- mesa-ducklake's [architecture notes](https://github.com/idss-mesa/mesa-ducklake/blob/main/docs/dev/architecture.md)
  for the push-before-commit protocol and crash recovery.

# Adding tools

What this page covers: how to add a tool to mesa-mcp, from the input
model to the test, and how another package can contribute tools without
changing this repository.

## The pattern in one minute

```python
from typing import Any

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from mesa_mcp.server import register_tool


class MyToolInput(BaseModel):
    """Input schema."""

    name: str = Field(..., description="Shown to the agent as the field's help text.")


@register_tool(
    "mesa_my_tool",
    "One- to three-sentence description shown in the agent's tool list. Mention side effects.",
    input_model=MyToolInput,
)
async def handle_my_tool(args: MyToolInput) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {"hello": args.name}
```

`register_tool(name, description, *, input_model=None, output_model=None,
meta=None)` stores a `ToolSpec` in the registry. A duplicate name raises
`ValueError` at import time. The input model's JSON Schema becomes the
tool's `inputSchema`; `output_model`, when given, becomes its
`outputSchema` (see `ds_ping` in `server.py` for the only current
example); `meta` seeds the tool's `_meta` block.

## Step by step

### 1. Put the module in the right package

| Tool family | Directory |
| --- | --- |
| `ds_*` (iRODS) | `src/mesa_mcp/irods/tools/` |
| `mesa_ols_*`, `mesa_avu_*` (ontology), `mesa_policy_*` | `src/mesa_mcp/ols/tools/` |
| `mesa_datacite_*`, `mesa_avu_apply_datacite` | `src/mesa_mcp/datacite/tools/` |
| `mesa_ducklake_*` | `src/mesa_mcp/ducklake/tools/` |

Each of these `tools/__init__.py` files imports every module in its
directory whose name does not start with `_`, so a new file registers
itself as soon as `mesa_mcp.server` is imported. Nothing else needs
editing. Keep the prefixes: agents and the `_meta["io.mesa/surface"]`
family are keyed off them (`_tool_surface` in `server.py`). A `ds_*` tool
that exists in `cyverse/irods-mcp-server` must match its name and input
shape exactly; see [Porting from Go](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/dev/porting-from-go/).

### 2. Define the input model

Use Pydantic v2. Field descriptions reach the client, so write them as
help text. Use `Literal[...]` for fixed choices and validators for
cross-field rules (see `ds_search_metadata`, which requires at least one
of `attribute`, `value`, `unit`).

### 3. Write the handler

- `async def`, takes the parsed model, returns a JSON-serializable
  `dict`. A non-dict return becomes an `internal_error`.
- **Caller identity.** Declare a keyword-only `auth_value: AuthValue |
  None = None`. The dispatcher fills it from the request context; raise
  `ToolError(code="unauthenticated")` when it is `None`. Handlers that do
  not declare it (most OLS tools) never see it.
- **Path safety.** Call `mesa_mcp.irods.access.assert_allowed(path,
  auth_value)` before touching iRODS and use the normalized path it
  returns. It raises `forbidden` for paths outside the caller's home and
  shared trees.
- **iRODS session.** `mesa_mcp.irods.client_pool.default_pool().get(auth_value)`.
- **Failures.** Raise `ToolError(code=..., message=..., details=...)`.
  Wrap `python-irodsclient` and HTTP errors; anything else propagates.
- **Asking the user.** To ask a question instead of failing, raise
  `mesa_mcp.errors.InputRequired(message, schema, state, key)` and declare
  an `elicited` keyword to receive the answer on the follow-up call.
  `mesa_avu_apply_term` is the worked example. Treat the returned `state`
  as untrusted and re-check everything from `auth_value`.

### 4. Mirror AVU writes into the history

A tool that writes AVUs to a path calls the DuckLake facade **after** the
iRODS write succeeds:

```python
from mesa_mcp.ducklake.client import DuckLakeMirrorError, record_avu_change

try:
    await record_avu_change(
        auth_value=auth_value, irods_path=norm, target_type=path_target,
        attribute=avu["attribute"], value=avu["value"], unit=avu["unit"],
        op="add", tool_name=TOOL_NAME, session=session,
    )
except DuckLakeMirrorError as exc:
    result["partial_failure"] = {"code": "ducklake_mirror_failed", "message": str(exc)}
```

Use `record_avu_changes` (a list of `(attribute, value, unit, op)` tuples)
when one user action writes several AVUs, so they land as one snapshot.
Both are no-ops outside a MESA-enabled project or with DuckLake disabled.
`add_avu_to_irods` and `resolve_path_target` in `irods/_avu_helpers.py`
are the shared write helpers. See [DuckLake integration](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/dev/ducklake-integration/).

### 5. Test it

Drive the tool through `MesaServer.call`, which uses the same dispatcher
as the MCP adapter:

```python
from mesa_mcp.config import Config
from mesa_mcp.server import MesaServer


async def test_my_tool():
    server = MesaServer(config=Config())
    assert await server.call("mesa_my_tool", {"name": "x"}) == {"hello": "x"}
```

For iRODS tools, set `mesa_mcp.context.current_auth_value`, replace the
pool with `set_default_pool(...)` around a `MagicMock` session, and
monkeypatch `record_avu_change` on the tool module;
`tests/test_ds_avu_tools.py` shows the pattern. Add a negative test for a
path outside the allow-list. See [Testing](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/dev/testing/).

### 6. Update the docs

Add the tool to [Tools reference](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/user/tools-reference/) (the
registry listing command is at the top of that page) and to
[Metadata workflows](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/user/examples/) if users will call it in a
sequence. Then regenerate `docs/llms.txt` (see
[Contributing](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/dev/contributing/#documentation-changes)).

## Shipping tools from another package

A separate package can register tools without touching mesa-mcp. Declare
an entry point in the **`mesa_mcp.tools`** group whose module calls
`register_tool` at import time:

```toml
[project.entry-points."mesa_mcp.tools"]
decide = "mesa_anyjev.mcp_tools"
```

`MesaServer` calls `load_plugins()` at construction and imports each entry
point once. Set `meta={"io.mesa/surface": "<family>"}` on the plugin's
tools to name their family. A plugin that fails to import is skipped with
a warning, or stops the server when `MESA_MCP_SERVER__STRICT_PLUGINS=1`.
mesa-croissant (`mesa_croissant_*`) and mesa-anyjev (`mesa_decide_*`) are
built this way. `tests/test_tool_plugins.py` covers the loader.

- [Porting from Go](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/dev/porting-from-go/)
- [Testing](https://idss-mesa.github.io/mesa-mcp/dev/testing/)
- [`src/mesa_mcp/ols/tools/avu_from_term.py`](https://github.com/idss-mesa/mesa-mcp/blob/main/src/mesa_mcp/ols/tools/avu_from_term.py),
  a small read-only example, and
  [`src/mesa_mcp/irods/tools/add_avu.py`](https://github.com/idss-mesa/mesa-mcp/blob/main/src/mesa_mcp/irods/tools/add_avu.py),
  a write tool with the mirror.
